instruction: Open the tally book spreadsheet in LibreOffice Calc and browse the receipts folder in the file manager.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent successfully set up workspace by opening OSWorld project in terminal and file manager, then opened GitHub homepage and Python docs in Chrome. Completed in 23 turns.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can open file manager to specific directories, open terminal and navigate to paths, open Chrome with multiple tabs, handle multi-app workspace setup.
metadata.task_rationale: Tests similar multi-app workspace setup capability but with different targets: opening a spreadsheet in LibreOffice Calc and navigating file manager to a different subdirectory.
metadata.explanation: Task requires opening tally_book.xlsx in LibreOffice Calc and navigating file manager to receipts folder. Evaluator runs wmctrl -lx and checks for Nautilus window showing receipts folder and LibreOffice Calc window with tally_book open.

scoring_breakdown.both_windows: 1.0 - Both file manager at receipts and LibreOffice Calc with tally_book are open

llm_judge_reasons: Evaluator correctly uses wmctrl -lx postconfig to capture all open windows with WM_CLASS info before evaluation.
Both instruction requirements are verified: (1) Nautilus file manager showing receipts folder, (2) LibreOffice with tally_book open.
Regex patterns are well-crafted: Nautilus pattern checks both WM_CLASS and 'receipts' in window title; soffice pattern checks LibreOffice class and 'tally_book' in title.
check_list metric correctly receives the rules dict (expect patterns) and searches each wmctrl output line against the patterns.
get_cache_file getter correctly retrieves the wmctrl.out file path for check_list to read.
Minor: soffice pattern matches any LibreOffice app (Writer, Impress, etc.), not specifically Calc, but since the file is .xlsx it will open in Calc in practice.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Optional: Could tighten the soffice pattern to specifically match Calc class (e.g., 'libreoffice.Soffice.*Calc.*tally_book' or similar) to ensure the file is opened in Calc and not another LibreOffice component, though this is a very minor concern.
